newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne slides further on ACCC talk.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne slides further on ACCC talk.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne Ltd's shares slid a further 20 cents or 2.1 percent to A$9.26 in active early Friday trade on increasing nervousness about the chances of regulatory approval for Westpac Banking Corp's A$9.75 a share takeover bid.
Brokers said a newspaper article interpreting comments by Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) Chairman Allan Fels as negative for the bid was the driving factor.
"The papers are saying the ACCC could be difficult (about the takeover) and that has seen some people get out," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.

The Australian Financial Review said on Friday Westpac's A$1.435 billion bid looked unlikely to succeed, interpreting comments by Fels late on Thursday as meaning he had not changed his late 1995 stance on the need for one regional bank per state.
A Westpac/Bank of Melbourne takeover would leave Victoria without a significant regional bank.
Fels said on Thursday the Wallis Financial System Inquiry seemed to agree with the ACCC about the importance of regional banks.
But he noted that some parts of the market had changed and the ACCC was now assessing whether there had been sufficient change for it to change its view.
Fels has said various times since last week's bid that he did not believe there had been sufficient change to justify a change in stance, but that he was prepared to hear Westpac's arguments.
